title: Momentum Ledger
tagline: What one 5-tonne catch-and-throw withdraws from the tether's orbit in joules and kilometres, and how long the installed power takes to put it back, for the Rev A ladder rather than the MXER draft.
pitch: finance/reboost_bound.py gives an energy bound for the non-canonical in-space fork (1.07 km/s tip, service_mxer_draft.json). This page does the same bookkeeping for the three Rev A tiers and extends it by one step. Column one: the payload's specific-energy gain from the lower-tip catch state (r = R - L, v = v_orb - v_tip) to the upper-tip release state (r = R + L, v = v_orb + v_tip), 43.0 MJ/kg = 11.95 kWh/kg at 2.5 km/s, 2.15e11 J per 5 t, shown beside the two other values the repo carries for the same quantity (finance/skyhook_finance.py line 215 uses 2 v_orb v_tip = 37.8 MJ/kg; MP-001 section 3a says 44.8 MJ/kg = 12.4 kWh/kg). Column two: a recovery-time grid over installed power (50 kW to 10 MW) x efficiency (0.15 / 0.26 / 0.40 from MP-001's ladder) x duty (0.3 / 0.5 as in reboost_bound.py), with the founding document's sizing rule (restore one design-payload boost within 5-10 days with 30 % margin) drawn as a band: 250 kW at 26 % takes 38 days, 1 MW 9.6 days, one catch per day needs about 9.6 MW electrical. Column three, the ledger: CoM delta-v per catch-and-throw by momentum conservation with the [Speculative] 200 t hub (30.8 m/s), the semi-major-axis and perigee drop (57 km, 114 km), the lower tip's perigee altitude afterwards (176 km), and how many un-reboosted catches reach a chosen tip-altitude floor.
whyNow: finance/reboost_bound.py and finance/REBOOST_BOUND_FINDINGS.md exist only for params/service_mxer_draft.json ('the full orbit-integrated ed_reboost.py remains the open workstream'); docs/project_instructions.md section 4.6 sizing requirement (5-10 days, 30 % margin) and section 4.2 'ballast mass improves catch dynamics'; docs/glossary.md 'Momentum bank / Momentum ledger'; docs/research/mp001_market_pricing.md section 3a (44.8 MJ/kg, 26 % efficiency); finance/skyhook_finance.py line 215 (2 v_orb v_tip MJ/kg); the three disagree.
computes: Inputs: snapshot orbital/geometry/kinematics, 5,000 kg tonnage payload, hub mass as an explicit [Speculative] input defaulting to the tether_dynamics 200 t, power/efficiency/duty sliders. Math: dE = m_p [(v_orb + v_tip)^2/2 - mu/(R + L) - (v_orb - v_tip)^2/2 + mu/(R - L)]; t_rec = dE/(P eta duty); dv_catch = m_p v_tip/(M + m_p), dv_throw = m_p v_tip/M, da = 2 R (dv_catch + dv_throw)/v_orb (tangential impulses at nearly the same orbital position, 6.7 min apart), perigee drop 2 da; the same function applied to the MXER draft reproduces reboost_bound's 1.056547e11 J. Outputs: energy table with the two discrepant repo values, recovery grid, ledger figures, catches-to-floor count. A Python CLI prints the grid in reboost_bound.py's format.
dataNeeded: snapshots/rev_a.json whole (about 7 KB) and snapshots/service_mxer_draft.json excerpted with --pick tether_com_orbit,tether,catch_origin,payload_class,capex_inputs (about 1.5 KB) for the cross-check; both via tools/snapshot.mjs.
existingOverlap: finance/reboost_bound.py (energy bound, MXER draft config only, GEO-transfer release model) and the in-page catch sketch's cosmetic 'ED reboost: ON' toggle. The program-site calculator computes reboost electricity $/kg from (v_rel^2 - (v_orb - v_tip)^2)/2 without the radius terms. Nothing computes Rev A per-catch energy at the tip radii, the recovery grid for the ladder, or the orbit drop per catch. This idea reuses reboost_bound's structure and vocabulary ([FLAGGED] brackets) so the maintainer can diff them.
honestyRisks: An energy bound is not a Lorentz-force model: plasma density, field geometry, current collection, eclipse and the angular-momentum restoration question are folded into efficiency and duty brackets exactly as reboost_bound.py flags them, and the page carries its scope line verbatim with provenance. The hub mass is [Speculative] and is a visible input, never a hidden constant; the perigee-drop treats catch and throw as co-located impulses and says so. No $/kg appears because rev_a.json has no electricity price. The three in-repo energy figures are reported as a reconciliation item with file and line, not adjudicated. The founding document's 5-10 day rule is quoted as a requirement.
testPlan: node --test and test_ledger.py: dE per kg at Rev A from the energy difference equals the work integral form to 1e-9 and is 43.0 MJ/kg within 0.1 % from snapshot inputs; the kernel applied to the MXER draft snapshot reproduces 1.056547e11 J within rel 1e-3 (reboost_bound.py's golden, as in tests/test_analysis_layer.py); recovery time is monotone decreasing in P, eta and duty; dv_catch + dv_throw = 30.8 m/s within 0.1 % for M_hub = 200 t and tends to zero as M_hub grows; perigee drop = 2 da; catches-to-floor is an integer that decreases with the floor altitude; the page shows a refusal for $/kg; smoke at 390 px.
landing: Skyhook, finance/reboost_bound_rev_a.py (sharing reboost_bound.py's table format) plus a REBOOST_BOUND_REV_A_FINDINGS.md, a derived `reboost.energy_per_catch_MJ_per_kg` entry in params/rev_a.json with confidence, and a reconciliation note for skyhook_finance.py line 215 and MP-001 section 3a. To ship: Rule 1 imports, a hub-mass budget to replace the 200 t placeholder, and the orbit-integrated ED model the external review asked for.
notes: Recomputed per-catch energy 43.03 MJ/kg vs skyhook_finance.py:215's 2·v_orb·v_tip = 37.78 and MP-001 §3a's 44.8: the three-way disagreement is real and unreconciled. reboost_bound.py covers only the MXER draft.

Verified finance/skyhook_finance.py:215 uses 2·v_orb·v_tip (37.8 MJ/kg), MP-001:37 states 44.8 MJ/kg, and reboost_bound's golden 1.056547e11 J is pinned in test_analysis_layer.py:77; the three-way disagreement is a real reconciliation item.

Three in-repo energy figures confirmed to disagree: the tip-radius difference gives 43.03 MJ/kg, finance/skyhook_finance.py:215 uses 2·v_orb·v_tip = 37.78, MP-001 line 37 states 44.8. reboost_bound.py's recovery_days and GEO-transfer scope confirmed; 200 t hub is a visible [Speculative] input.
